I believe a conservative ray-guided navigator with filtered sensors and bug-style wall following will generalise across layouts, so I am adding target steering, adaptive compass correction, obstacle bypassing, stuck recovery, and checkpoint-aware speed control.

I believe attempt 3 was trapped by aggressive compass-driven oscillation and sticky ray state, so this version blends GPS course with filtered heading, brakes earlier, follows one obstacle side persistently, and switches sides only when the chosen gap is pinched.

I believe the rover was getting trapped by stale obstacle readings, excessive angular momentum, and recovery spins, so this version releases sensors faster, damps heading rate strongly, and uses persistent but more stable wall following with a straight reverse escape.

I believe the earlier runs were trapped by excessive differential-spin and stale reactive steering, so this version uses a slower persistent bug-style wall follower with short sensor memory, GPS/compass fusion, controlled escape maneuvers, and stronger boundary protection.
